status_summary: In the successor structure the trade-and-investment direction exists but the named vehicle shrank: State's Bureau of African Affairs launched a commercial diplomacy strategy on 2025-05-14 that makes advocacy for US business a core measure for ambassadors, names Commerce as a partner and calls for overhauling US trade promotion and financing tools, DFC reached financial close with the Development Bank of Southern Africa on 786 million dollars for the Lobito Corridor railway (reported 2026-08-04), and a US-DRC strategic partnership signed 2025-12-04 gives US persons first-offer rights on strategic mineral projects and promotes the Sakania-Lobito corridor. Prosper Africa was not expanded: a 2025-02-06 report said it was shut down with USAID's dismantling, and CSIS (2025-12-19) and African Business (2026-03-16) reported that its USAID-housed Africa Trade and Investment Activity was terminated, with no source stating the initiative's current status. No explicit measure holding China accountable for extractive investment, and no program building on church, philanthropic or diaspora initiatives, was found. The stage is in_progress because the commercial-diplomacy and DFC elements are operative, at a lower progress figure because the text's named step, expanding Prosper Africa, moved the other way.

timeline.event: Launch Base Africa reported that Prosper Africa had been shut down amid the dismantling of USAID, with its website under maintenance and its future uncertain.

State's acting senior Africa official launched the Bureau of African Affairs commercial diplomacy strategy at a business summit in Abidjan, listing six actions that include making commercial diplomacy a core focus and reforming US trade promotion, project preparation and financing tools; Reuters reported he said envoys would be judged on business deals rather than aid.

The United States and the Democratic Republic of the Congo signed a strategic partnership on critical minerals, infrastructure and governance, with US first-offer rights on strategic mineral projects and support for the Sakania-Lobito corridor.
DFC announced that the FY2026 NDAA, signed that day per its release, reauthorized DFC through 2031-12-31 and raised its maximum contingent liability to 205 billion dollars.
CSIS reported that Prosper Africa's USAID-housed Africa Trade and Investment Activity ended with USAID's dissolution.

timeline.event: African Business described Prosper Africa as a coordinating platform and reported that its main implementing activity, the USAID Africa Trade and Investment activity, was terminated ahead of schedule after the 2025 foreign assistance review, without naming a successor.
Engineering News reported that DFC and the Development Bank of Southern Africa reached financial close on a $786 million Lobito Corridor railway project run by Mota-Engil and Trafigura.

title: Build Africa policy on trade and investment: expand Prosper Africa, hold China accountable
uncertainties: No State, Commerce, DFC or White House statement on the formal end or continuation of Prosper Africa was found (one further search in review); the 2025 Launch Base Africa report, CSIS and African Business are the evidence, and African Business describes the initiative in the present tense without confirming it operates. The AllAfrica transcript carries no date in its text; the launch date 2025-05-14 is inferred from the Reuters report, which says the launch was on a Wednesday and is dated 2025-05-15. The transcript names Commerce and China but not DFC, Treasury or Prosper Africa. The DRC agreement summary read (IEA tracker) does not mention China. The August 2026 Lobito report does not state DFC's share. The DFC release does not state the NDAA signing date directly; it says the law was signed the day of the release. A US-Africa Leaders Summit and the June 2025 US-Africa Business Summit outcomes were not verified. AGOA is tracked in c09-06 and DFC reform in c09-08; Somaliland and the wider China agenda in Africa in c06-15.
